parts.transcriptHtml:
Tutor: Come in!

Ahmed: Hi.

Tutor: Oh, hello, Ahmed... how are you?

Ahmed: Fine, thanks.

Tutor: Have a seat. So... how do you think the seminar went last week?

Ahmed: {[Oh, well... I enjoyed it, yes, though I'm not sure I really followed parts of the discussion that took place -- you know, about the theory and all that...][1]}

Tutor: Well, we can talk about that later... but were you comfortable in a group?

Ahmed: Oh, it's better, I think, than working on your own -- though you're comparing yourself all the time with the other students there.

Tutor: OK, well, let's talk about how you did and look at some strategies to help you in the future.

Ahmed: That would be great.

Tutor: Now, one of the things that students often overlook when they go to seminars is that you do need to prepare for them. You can't rely on other people.

Ahmed: {[I know, and I did look at the results of the experiments we did in class and write them up beforehand... as you said.][2]}

Tutor: {[Yes... and that was good, it made it easier to analyse them.][2]} But you have to do some background reading as well. Did you get the list of articles I sent round?

Ahmed: Mmm - I've started to read them...

Tutor: OK, well, you'll know that for next time.

Ahmed: Yes, yes, sure.

Tutor: So let's move on to your participation in the seminar.

Ahmed: Right.

Tutor: Perhaps you can tell me how you think that went?

Ahmed: Yeah, well, I'm not used to talking to more than a couple of people - it's very different from the way we learn in my home country.

Tutor: Yes, I appreciate that.

Ahmed: So I think I, um... well, I know I should have included everyone, {[but I think I kept turning to the person next to me.][3]}

Tutor: Is that because you were avoiding eye contact?

Ahmed: I don't think so - I'm not shy - it's just habit, I think.

Tutor: Well, that will improve as we do more seminars.

Ahmed: Uh-huh.

Tutor: Um, another difficulty is knowing when to speak.

Ahmed: Like when it's your turn?

Tutor: Yes.

Ahmed: I felt I did wait for a pause...

Tutor: Yes, you handled that quite well.

Ahmed: The thing I'm really concerned about is keeping up with the discussion.

Tutor: Ah, does your mind wander off?

Ahmed: Sometimes. I jot down a lot of information, {[but I still find myself thinking about something else when lots of other students are talking.][4]}

Tutor: Mmm. If there's an assignment to do at the end of a group, that usually helps!

Ahmed: I'm sure it does.

Tutor: OK. Now, the last thing I want to look at is the role that you play in the seminar.

Ahmed: What do you mean?

Tutor: Well, when students work in groups, they don't all behave the same way. Some students are quiet, some look for support, some ask a lot of questions...

Ahmed: {[Oh... that's a new idea to me. I don't know what I'm like...][5]}

Tutor: That's probably because you're thinking about your own performance all the time.

Ahmed: I guess so. I mean, should I be different in some way.

Tutor: {[What I would say is that when we do the next seminar, you should look more at the people around you... you know, look outside yourself.][6]}

Ahmed: Like, ask myself how they feel?

Tutor: Yes, or what they're looking for from the group.

Ahmed: OK.

Tutor: It doesn't take much, but it's important to watch what other students are doing.

Ahmed: OK, I'll do that.

Tutor: Fine. Now,...

(Pause)

Tutor: Now, I'm going to suggest a couple of strategies for next week's seminar.

Ahmed: OK - that's great. I need to participate more.

Tutor: Well, it's not a question of saying more - but we need everyone to feel comfortable about giving their views.

Ahmed: Then the discussion is better.

Tutor: Yes. So... you're a confident person...

Ahmed: Should I make sure I'm near someone who's quiet?

Tutor: You can do, {[but it's more about how well you pay attention to other students.][7]}

Ahmed: OK - so I need to be attentive.

Tutor: {[Yes, and then encourage someone else to say more by saying: 'What did you mean when you said...?' or 'What do you think about the idea that...?'][8]}

Ahmed: That way I'm talking...

Tutor: Yes, but you'll find that other people will talk, too. You'll all start to get really involved.

Ahmed: Right - they're good suggestions.

Tutor: The other thing that can really help is the way you take notes.

Ahmed: Yeah, I know I write down everything, but I should be stricter with myself.

Tutor: {[Well, you actually need to think a few days ahead.][9]}

Ahmed: Really?

Tutor: Yes - 'What's the topic?' and 'What's the best way of making notes?'

Ahmed: I see. So I have a strategy when I walk in the room.

Tutor: Exactly. Then, when you read through them later, they'll make sense and you won't have to write them out again.

Ahmed: I always have to do that!

Tutor: {[The other thing I would say is that you should include a small column in your notes where you can jot down things you want to go back to before the seminar ends.][10]}

Ahmed: Like a reminder.

Tutor: Yes. Notes aren't just for later - you can use them as a prompt when there's a pause in the discussion.

Ahmed: That's been really helpful.

Tutor: OK - see you in class tomorrow.

Ahmed: Thanks.

questionSets.title: Questions 21-26
questionSets.instructionHtml: Question 1-6: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.text: What does Ahmed say about last week's seminar?

options.text: He wasn't able to get there on time.
He didn't know all the students.

questions.text: What does the tutor say about Ahmed's preparation for the seminar?

options.text: He was better prepared than some students.

questions.text: What does Ahmed say about his participation in the seminar?

options.text: He tended to speak to his neighbour only.
He spoke when other students were talking.
He felt embarrassed when students looked at him.

questions.text: What does Ahmed worry about most in seminars?
What does Ahmed say about his role in the group?

options.text: He feels he is acting a part.

questions.text: At the next seminar, Ahmed's tutor suggests that he should

options.text: give other students more help with their work.
observe the behaviour of other students.
ask other students for their views.

questions.text: Which TWO strategies does the tutor suggest for the next seminar? Choose TWO letters, A- E.

options.text: listen to what other people say

questions.text: Which TWO suggestions does the tutor make about taking notes? Choose TWO letters, A-E.

options.text: note down key words that people say
